NOTICE.TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2024/811 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 March 2024 on anti-money laundering requirements for credit institutions and financial undertakings
NOTICE.CONTENTS:
Article 1 - Subject matter and scope. This Regulation lays down rules regarding the customer due diligence measures to be applied by credit institutions and financial undertakings when establishing and maintaining business relationships. It applies to all obliged entities as defined in Directive (EU) 2015/849.
Article 2 - Definitions. For the purposes of this Regulation: (a) 'customer due diligence' means the process of identifying and verifying the identity of a customer and beneficial owner, understanding the nature and purpose of the business relationship, and conducting ongoing monitoring; (b) 'beneficial owner' means any natural person who ultimately owns or controls a customer and on whose behalf a transaction or activity is being conducted.
Article 3 - Customer due diligence measures. 1. Obliged entities shall apply customer due diligence measures when establishing a business relationship. 2. Customer due diligence measures shall consist of: (a) identifying the customer and verifying the customer's identity on the basis of documents, data or information obtained from a reliable and independent source; (b) identifying the beneficial owner and taking reasonable measures to verify that person's identity so that the obliged entity is satisfied that it knows who the beneficial owner is; (c) assessing and, as appropriate, obtaining information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship; (d) conducting ongoing monitoring of the business relationship.
Article 4 - Enhanced due diligence. 1. In cases referred to in Articles 18 to 24 of Directive (EU) 2015/849, obliged entities shall apply enhanced customer due diligence measures. 2. Enhanced due diligence shall include at minimum: (a) obtaining additional information on the customer and on the beneficial owner; (b) obtaining additional information on the intended nature of the business relationship; (c) obtaining information on the source of funds and source of wealth of the customer and of the beneficial owner; (d) conducting enhanced ongoing monitoring of the business relationship by increasing the number and timing of controls applied, and selecting patterns of transactions that need further examination.
Article 5 - Simplified due diligence. Simplified due diligence may be applied where the business relationship or transaction presents a lower degree of risk. In such cases, obliged entities may apply simplified customer due diligence measures as set out in Annex I to this Regulation.
Article 6 - Record keeping. Obliged entities shall retain copies of the documents and information obtained during the customer due diligence process for a period of five years after the termination of the business relationship.
Article 7 - Reporting obligations. 1. Member States shall ensure that obliged entities report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) without delay. 2. Obliged entities shall refrain from carrying out the transaction they suspect to be related to money laundering before informing the FIU.
Article 8 - Entry into force. This Regulation shall enter into force on 1 July 2024. It shall apply from that date.
